title: WeDesign: Generative AI–Facilitated Community Consultations for Urban Public Space Design

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative analysis of workshop prompts and text-to-image outputs, noting the model's failure to depict functionally accurate accessibility features (e.g., ramp slopes, pavement gradients) and its tendency to insert tokenistic representations like random wheelchairs.

Evaluation of participant feedback and generated images, observing the model's inability to accurately render specific local architectural cues (Montreal) and its tendency to default to generic or European cityscapes.

Analysis of workshop transcripts and prompt logs, highlighting how the model performed poorly with French prompts, forcing francophone participants to use English to achieve contextually relevant results.

Qualitative review of images generated from prompts requesting diverse ethnic backgrounds, finding that the model often relied on tokenistic elements (e.g., symbolic flags) rather than organic, authentic representation.
